archetypes.name: code-robustness
archetypes.rationale: The diff introduces new shell scripts with temp-file atomicity patterns (mv -f), global variable mutation across function boundaries in persist-retally-step3-env.sh, multi-path awk/Python fallback chains, and a tally-error cleanup ordering that depends on _RESOLVED_ROUND_NUM being set correctly before consumers run.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine write-design-round-meta.sh for temp-file atomicity: verify that _panel_tmp and _meta_tmp are always cleaned up on failure paths and that the mv -f from tmp to final is not silently dropped when mv itself fails. Examine the global variable handoff in persist-retally-step3-env.sh: _RESOLVED_ROUND_NUM and _RESOLVED_ROUND_DIR are set by _resolve_retally_round and consumed later by _rollback_mav_round_state and _clear_design_round_meta_on_tally_error; check whether any early-exit path between _resolve_retally_round and those consumers could leave the globals unset and cause silent no-ops. Review the IFS=$'\t' read order in write-design-round-meta.sh against the awk printf column order to confirm NEUTRAL_COUNT and EXONERATED_COUNT are not transposed. Check compose-review-findings.sh: the _design_filtered temp file is removed inside the fi block, but if filter_design_gate_b_skipped fails and returns non-zero, the cleanup path and the fallback to the original _design_accepted must be traced to ensure no dangling temp file or wrong accepted file is used. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
